newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland's Rosati sticks by 2000 target date for EU.
newsitem.headline: Poland's Rosati sticks by 2000 target date for EU.

text.p: Poland's foreign minister, reacting on Wednesday to a European Commission statement that no new countries were likely to enter the Union before 2002, said Warsaw still saw the year 2000 as its target date.

"This is not the first statement...in which Brussels bureaucrats say it will be hard for central European countries to enter the European Union before the year 2002," the minister, Dariusz Rosati, told a regular news briefing.

"Our plan is clear, we want to enter the Union in 2000," Rosati said, adding that this was a realistic goal but that it was more important for Poland to win good conditions than to get in by a set moment.

"We have a plan, the year 2000. But, frankly, if I had to decide whether to enter in 2000 on poorer terms or in 2001 on better terms, I would prefer 2001," Rosati said. He had been asked to comment on the statement, which the Commission later withdrew, saying that it did not reflect its official position.
Commission spokesman Thierry Daman told Reuters in Brussels
